calls.title: Growthbook <> Kiosk - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: The team discussed a new pricing model that shifts to a platform plus per-user fee structure, reducing the base cost to $40,000 and allowing for $100 per user monthly. This aligns with client needs to avoid high upfront fees while ensuring scalable billing. Initial onboarding plans target three clients, projecting two active clients by year-end, with contracts averaging over five years. Competitor comparisons highlighted differences in pricing and offerings, with GrowthBook focusing on experimentation features compared to Dynamic Yield and Convert. A demo is scheduled to evaluate GrowthBook’s front-end capabilities and influence future negotiations, amidst operational needs for separate client data management to ensure compliance.
calls.keywords: Enterprise Pricing, Experimentation Platform, Contextual Bandits, AI-driven Testing, Client Scalability, Competitor Comparison

calls.title: Growthbook <> Kiosk - V/E Demo - POC Scoping
calls.summary: The meeting provided a comprehensive overview of Growth Book's Visual Editor, highlighting its AI-assisted features like dynamic JavaScript execution, manual selectors, and integration with Google Analytics for enhanced reporting. Participants, including Graham McNicoll and John Devoy, discussed the importance of firm pricing discussions, with an emphasis on a preferred self-hosted solution contingent on competitive pricing. The need for collaboration with design and engineering teams was acknowledged to maintain branding standards, while the significance of experimentation best practices was emphasized, particularly the recommendation of a two-week minimum duration for statistical relevance. The team expressed enthusiasm regarding upcoming features like contextual bandits for optimized traffic allocation based on user attributes, and plans for trial preparations and resource sharing were established.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, Visual Editor, A/B testing, GA4 integration, multi-armed bandits, cloud vs self-hosted

calls.title: Growthbook <> Kiosk - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: The team discussed a competitive pricing model, offering a final price of $21,000 for up to 10 users on a self-hosted plan. This price is a substantial reduction from the original mid-$40,000 range, requiring onboarding of three clients, with intent from two additional clients within 60 days to mitigate risk. They aim for a phased rollout, addressing client operational needs with flexible user seat arrangements. A demo of the Extra Bandit product is expected within 1–2 weeks, aligning with client timelines despite a slight project delay. Clear communication, via a detailed cost summary email from Dan Wathne to Mark Nelson, is crucial for internal review and ensuring commitment before the intended deal closure in July.
calls.keywords: Pricing, onboarding, client commitments, phased rollout, demo availability, platform fee
